## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Maṇikuṇḍalajātaka* (Ja 351) is a birth story belonging to the *Catukkanipāta* of the Pali Jātaka collection [Fausböll 1883]. The narrative frame opens at the Jetavana monastery, where the Buddha recounts the story regarding a councillor guilty of misconduct within the harem of the king of Kosala [Fausböll 1883]. In the past narrative, the Bodhisatta reigns as the king of Bārāṇasī, whose treacherous minister brings the king of Kosala to capture the kingdom of Kāsi and imprison the Bodhisatta [Fausböll 1883]. The opening verse incipit is noted in the commentary as *Jino rathassa maṇikuṇḍalā ca 'ti* [Fausböll 1883]. The text is also included in modern canonical selections of wisdom verses [Anandajoti 2010].

 Computational analysis by DharmaNexus confirms these internal Pali correspondences, identifying extensive text reuse between the *Maṇikuṇḍalajātaka* and the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Jarāsuttaniddesa* (segments 2.1–3.4), the *Attadaṇḍasuttaniddesa* (segments 0.4–3.4), the *Bhūripaññajātaka* (Ja 452, segments 4.1–5.4), and the *Cariyāpiṭaka-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus identifies automatic cross-language alignments with the Tibetan translation of the *Ārya-vīradattagṛhaparipṛcchā-nāma-mahāyānasūtra* (D0072) and the Sanskrit *Patna Dharmapada* [DharmaNexus].
